title: The front page, round 2: who wrote it, said plainly; what makes us different, first
summary: synthetic@'s run 6 read the three mock-ups of round 1 and found four things wrong with them. Round 2 fixes them: every byline names the AI agent that wrote the story (F35, blocking), 'every fact sourced' and who writes and edits come first (F36), a phone shows the readable article card, not the dense AI infographic (F37), and B, ranked last by all four readers, is dropped (F38).

steps.label: Round 2: A, the newspaper
steps.note: Bylines name the agent ('journalist-europe@web-summit.vicky, an AI agent, for Vicky Wang'); a band under the top says every fact is sourced and dated, written by AI agents, edited by Dinis Cruz, Indi Gupte and Vicky Wang, independent of Web Summit; Reach, Mandate, Gap right after the lead on a phone.

steps.label: Round 1: C, for comparison
steps.note: Round 1's briefing first, with the bylines that hid the agents.

steps.label: Round 2: C, the briefing first
steps.note: The same fixes on the briefing-first layout; on a phone the lead shows the article's card image, with the AI infographic one tap inside.

notes: F35 (blocking, synthetic@ run 6): round 1 wrote 'Vicky Wang's desk' or 'PrompTugal.news' where an AI agent wrote the story; a reader took it for a person. Round 2 prints the agent's own name from the article's author line, then 'an AI agent', then who it was for. My mistake, and the rule now: a byline never hides an agent.

F36: round 1 moved what makes the site different to the bottom and shrank 'Every fact sourced' to a grey line. Round 2 puts one band under the top, on every size: sourced and dated, written by AI agents and edited by three named people, independent.

F37: the AI infographic is too dense for a phone and two readers doubted it. On a phone the lead shows the session 1 card image (large type, every word checked), with the infographic one tap inside; on a desktop the infographic keeps a caption: AI-made, every figure checked, the dates are the mission's own.
F38: B, the visual wall, was ranked last by all four readers (bare figures with no source read as marketing). Dropped.
My pick stays A, now with the band; the choice is Dinis's.
